items.title: Afghan women tell the BBC their lives are unrecognisable after five years of Taliban rule
items.description: Women across the country speak of public floggings, losing their jobs, and barriers to healthcare that endanger lives.

items.title: Instagram accounts fuelling Ceuta crisis with paid advice for help to cross
items.description: BBC's Top Comment podcast has found a network of Instagram profiles glamourising the swim around the Morocco-Ceuta border fence.

items.title: Activists try to deliver aid to Palestinians in homes besieged by Israeli settlers
items.description: Two families have been trapped in their homes in the occupied West Bank for several days.

items.title: 'Unprecedented' rain in Japan kills eight people
items.description: The storm cut power to more than 20,000 households and left 7,000 people stranded at Tokyo's Narita airport.

items.title: Builders unearth €9m gold stash sealed in walls of Belgian property
items.description: Construction workers found the stash in the walls of a cellar while drilling to lay sewage pipes.

items.title: Stolen Matisse artworks recovered by police in Brazil
items.description: A man is arrested after eight works by the French artist are found at a home in greater São Paulo.

items.title: Dozens injured and thousands evacuated in Croatia wildfire
items.description: Officials say the blaze, near the port town of Omis, is one of the worst in Croatia's history.

items.title: France's top court blocks social media ban for under-15s
items.description: The Constitutional Council says it infringes upon freedom of expression - but President Macron vows to prepare a new draft.

items.title: Trump asks Supreme Court to allow ballroom work to continue
items.description: Forcing the US president to go "hat-in-hand to Congress" for permission would be "dangerous", the administration says.

items.title: Zambia vote counting resumes after pause over alleged attacks on polling staff
items.description: The electoral commission said violence had "resulted in the theft of marked ballot papers".

items.title: UK diplomats no longer get hardship bonus for being posted to Buenos Aires
items.description: Civil servants are entitled to extra money for working in difficult or dangerous cities around the world.

items.title: Conditions on US aircraft carrier at sea for more than 250 days raise alarms
items.description: Thousands of sailors on the USS Abraham Lincoln have reportedly faced food shortages and broken plumbing, with some considering jumping overboard.
